summary: Real progress in seat mode. The blue pillow now reads royal blue in the cabin (q08 #4956a4 vs tpg_42 #3a53a7; pillow/back fabric 1.03 in q08 and 0.76 in q09, was 1.34; photos 0.56-0.84). The white pillow stands behind and offset toward the aisle, showing on the top and aisle side only, as in omaat_room_15. The E pillows are square, the bundle sits at the cushion front, the slipper pack is a navy pouch, the monitor frame reaches the cabinet top (tpg_53), and the centre divider is two slim charcoal fins. What still breaks the photo match: (1) The pillow 'flange' is a separate flat plate with square corners in lilac (jPillowBack gRBox, r 0.045 clamped by its 8 mm thickness) behind a round-cornered cushion. In r7, r9 and r10 it reads as a cushion lying on a tray. omaat_room_15 shows a pillowcase whose grey flange (#a8a5b0 lit, #676880 shade) is continuous with a near-square-cornered pillow. (2) Bed mode is better than w7, but the duvet still reads as a thin T-shaped cut sheet: straight edges, sharp right-angle corners at the table notch, about 2 cm thick, no quilting (r9 close-up). tpg_70 and tpg_72 show a thick quilted comforter on a ~0.3 m stitched grid, with irregular soft edges and a visible check jacquard. (3) The ash grain is still about a quarter of the photo contrast: high-pass SD is 1.9-2.6% in q07 against 8.7% on the c_27316 cabinet door and 12-16% on the c_27316 and tpg_53 tables. Close up it reads as white plaster. (4) In bed mode the white pillow stands almost upright (-68 deg) and reads as a white headboard; in tpg_70 and tpg_72 it is propped low with the blue one lying on it. Lighting (not scored): the charcoal and fabric parts carry a blue cast (q10 back fabric #636a76 vs c_27315 #605d6b).

issues.detail: Pillow flange is a square-cornered lilac plate under a round-cornered cushion, so the pillow reads as a cushion on a tray
issues.problem: roomPillow adds the flange as gRBox(0.456, 0.008, 0.356, 0.045, 1) in jPillowBack #595b7e. With 8 mm thickness the 0.045 radius is clamped, so the plate has square corners, while the cushion loft has r 0.05 rounded corners. In r7, r9 and r10 the lilac plate shows as a separate rectangle around and under the pillow. In omaat_room_15 the pillow is a pillowcase with near-square corners and a ~2-3 cm flat flange continuous with the body, in neutral grey (#a8a5b0 lit, #676880 shade), lighter than the blue. It is not lilac.
issues.evidence: r7 crop: the plate corners stick out about 3 cm beyond the cushion's rounded corners. r9: the plate is visible below the bed pillow. omaat_room_15 crop (600-1000, 400-800): grey flange running along the top and right edges with tight corners.
issues.fix: 09c_room.js roomPillow: make body and flange share one outline. Body: cushionSecs(0.42, 0.32, 0.05, 0, { edge: 0.04, r: 0.025, crown: 0.014 }), with corner r 0.05 -> 0.025. Flange: replace the gRBox with B.add(gLoft(cushionSecs(0.46, 0.36, 0.006, -0.006, { edge: 0.003, r: 0.03 }), 2), xf, SEATMAT.jPillowBack). jPillowBack (09c local) c '#595b7e' -> '#85848c' (neutral grey, r 0.75).

issues.detail: Bed duvet reads as a thin cut sheet: straight edges, square corners at the table notch, no quilting, no jacquard
issues.problem: duvetSheet maps a regular u,v grid onto bounds(z), so the outline is exactly the plan bounds: a straight head edge, a straight outer edge, and a right-angle step where the bed narrows beside the table (smooth(-0.68, -0.60)). The cloth is only t = 0.02 thick, the fold field has no quilt stitching, and SEATMAT.duvet uses LAYER.fabric (plain). tpg_70 and tpg_72 show a thick, puffy comforter with a stitched grid of about 0.30-0.35 m, irregular sagging edges that cross the table notch diagonally, and the same check jacquard as the pillow.
issues.evidence: r9 close-up: T-shaped flat blue sheet with crisp 90-degree corners and a uniform 2 cm edge. tpg_72: diagonal edges, quilt channels about 1/3 of the bed width apart, and duvet colour #6f7cd9 with a visible check.
issues.fix: 09c_room.js duvetSheet: (a) puffiness: add f += 0.022 * smooth(0, 0.07, Math.min(x - xl, mr - x, zh, (hd > 0 ? z1 - z : z - z0))) so the cloth domes about 2 cm away from its edges, and t 0.02 -> 0.012 for the skirt. (b) quilting: in rotated cloth coordinates (q1 = x*cos(8deg) + z*sin(8deg), q2 = -x*sin + z*cos), f -= 0.012 * (Math.exp(-((q1 - 0.33*Math.round(q1/0.33))/0.012)**2) + Math.exp(-((q2 - 0.33*Math.round(q2/0.33))/0.012)**2)). Raise nu/nv 22/40 -> 40/72 so the grooves resolve. (c) irregular outline: in at(), xl += 0.03*Math.sin(5.3*z + 0.7), xr += 0.025*Math.sin(4.1*z + 2.0), and the head/foot z edges get + 0.03*Math.sin(9*u). Widen the table-notch blend from smooth(-0.68, -0.60) to smooth(-0.80, -0.50) so the edge runs diagonally under the table, as in tpg_72. (d) 09_seats.js (shared, one key): duvet l: LAYER.fabric -> LAYER.yagasuri.

issues.detail: Pillow check jacquard is coarse and faint
issues.problem: The real pillow has a bold ichimatsu checkerboard of about 1.5 cm squares in two clearly different blues. The render shows about 4-5 cm blotchy squares at low contrast (r7 crop).

issues.detail: Monument top reads as one wide charcoal beam across both columns (q09)
issues.problem: The monitor monument body gRBox(1.13, ..., 0.245) has one flat top across both columns, so in q09 a broad beam crosses the centre pair, with the new fins dwarfed beside it. In c_27313 and c_27314 the centre spine splits two separate dark monument boxes, and the fins with silver top edges rise flush with them.
issues.evidence: q09 crop: the beam is about 75 px wide against a 0.55 m table at about 200 px, so about 0.2 m. c_27313 crop shows a narrow slit and spine between two boxes.
issues.fix: 09c_room.js roomPart: split the monument into two bodies with a 0.05 gap at x of the centre spine (one per column), with a SEATMAT.jVoid strip in the gap, and give each top a 0.01 jPanelEdge lip. [A]: verify the spine x against c_27313 before cutting.
